_readme: Known symbols for ES1's DBSIM.EXE (ES1DBSIM): confirmed address -> meaning mappings, applied to the ES1Recon Ghidra project by ES2ApplySymbolNames.java.
Addresses are offsets into the flat X-32 image (Herculan/docs/es1/formats/x32-executable.md#the-image).
Schema, confidence rules and run order: tools/ghidra_scripts/README.md, 'Known symbols'.
Entries are in address order. tools/scripts/es2_naming.py insert and edit keep it, and check that it holds.

entries.name: X32_AllocMemory
entries.description: (size), C convention: rounds size up to a multiple of 0x1000 and asks the extender for that much memory (INT 21h AX=350Ch). On carry it returns -1; otherwise it stores EDX at 00090024, raises the high-water mark 00090028 to the block's end when the end is above it, and returns the block's address. Mem_InitHeap takes the heap's block from it, and operator new and malloc fall back on it while the heap is off.

entries.name: __x386_coproc_init
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `__x386_coproc_init`, from `x386.asm`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 86 bytes from here.

entries.name: Subsystem_RunPhase
entries.description: (phase), callee-cleaned: calls, in order, each function of the 6-byte {function, int16 phase} records at 000bbcb0 (count int16 0009011c) whose phase matches. Sim_RenderFrame runs phase 5. ES2's Subsystem_RunPhase (DBSIM 00401d94).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00000af4, against ES2's Subsystem_RunPhase

entries.name: Heap_Init
entries.description: (heap, block, size), callee-cleaned: sets up the heap object over the block: +0 base, +4 the size as given, +8 the free list (the block, its next link zeroed), and +0xc (free bytes) and +0x10 (their low mark) the size rounded down to a multiple of 8, which also becomes the block's size. Tags the block FBLK at +8.

entries.name: Heap_IsBlock
entries.description: (heap, block header): 1 when the address lies from the heap's base to 0x10 bytes before its end and carries a block tag (FBLK at +8 or ABLK at +0), else 0.

entries.name: Heap_LargestFree
entries.description: (heap), callee-cleaned: the largest size on the heap's free list (+8) less the 8-byte header, reading the list's head without testing it for null. Arena_Push sizes its arena with it on the heap 000ae4ac. ES1GO's Heap_LargestFree (00001091); ES2's Memory_LargestFreeBlock (DBSIM 00476dd0) subtracts 0x6c and clamps at 0.

entries.name: Heap_Alloc
entries.description: (heap, trackLow, size), callee-cleaned: first-fit allocation. Returns 0 for size 0. Rounds size + 8 up to a multiple of 8 and walks the free list (+8): a block of exactly that size is unlinked; a block more than 0x10 bytes larger is split, the tail staying on the list tagged FBLK; a block larger by 0x10 or less is passed over. The block is tagged ABLK, its payload zero-filled, its size taken off the free bytes (+0xc), and with trackLow set the low mark (+0x10) lowered to the free bytes. Returns the payload (header + 8), or 0 when no block fits.

entries.name: Heap_Free
entries.description: (heap, payload), callee-cleaned: nothing for a null payload. Adds the block's size back to the free bytes (+0xc), tags it FBLK, inserts it into the free list (+8) in address order, and merges it with the free block before it and the one after it where they touch.

entries.name: Heap_Realloc
entries.description: (heap, size, payload), callee-cleaned: size 0 frees the block (Heap_Free) and returns 0. A smaller size gives the tail back in place: to the free block that follows when there is one, otherwise as a new block freed through Heap_Free when the tail exceeds 0x10 bytes, and by moving the data into a new block (Heap_Alloc, memmove, Heap_Free) when it does not. A larger size takes the difference from a following free block large enough for it, and otherwise moves the data. The block after it is checked with Heap_IsBlock and its predecessor on the free list found with Heap_FindPrevFree. Lowers the low mark (+0x10) to the free bytes. Returns the payload, moved or not, or 0 when a move cannot allocate.

entries.name: Heap_FindPrevFree
entries.description: (heap, block): the free block whose next link is the given block, walking the list from +8; 0 when the block heads the list or the walk ends without finding it.

entries.name: Mem_InitHeap
entries.description: (size): caps size at X32_LargestFreeBlock() - 25000, takes a block that large from X32_AllocMemory, asserting 'Memory alloc failed' (memory.cpp line 504, severity 5) through Assert_Report when it returns -1, makes it the heap 000ae4ac (Heap_Init) and sets 000901d4, which sends operator new, malloc and the frees to the heap.

entries.name: Mem_HeapOff
entries.description: Clears 000901d4, after which operator new and malloc take memory from X32_AllocMemory and the frees do nothing.

entries.name: operator_new
entries.description: The game's operator new (size), callee-cleaned (RET 4): Heap_Alloc(000ae4ac, 1, size) while 000901d4 is set, otherwise X32_AllocMemory(size) with -1 returned as 0. It is the allocation a constructor makes for a null this (Herculan/docs/es1/formats/compiler.md#constructors-and-destructors). malloc is the same body with the C convention.

entries.name: Mem_AllocFromHeap
entries.description: (heap, size), callee-cleaned (RET 8): Heap_Alloc(heap, 1, size) on the heap it is given.

entries.name: operator_delete
entries.description: The game's operator delete (pointer), callee-cleaned (RET 4): Heap_Free(000ae4ac, pointer) while 000901d4 is set, otherwise nothing. It is the release a destructor makes when bit 0 of its flags is set (Herculan/docs/es1/formats/compiler.md#constructors-and-destructors). free is the same body with the C convention.

entries.name: malloc
entries.description: The game's malloc (size), C convention: operator_new's body, returning with a plain RET. It is the _malloc of the startup's argument vector (Herculan/docs/es1/formats/compiler.md#startup).

entries.name: free
entries.description: The game's free (pointer), C convention: operator_delete's body, returning with a plain RET.

entries.name: realloc
entries.description: The game's realloc (pointer, size), C convention: Heap_Realloc(000ae4ac, size, pointer), whether or not 000901d4 is set.

entries.name: calloc
entries.description: The game's calloc (count, size), C convention: count * size bytes from Heap_Alloc(000ae4ac, 1, ...) while 000901d4 is set, otherwise from X32_AllocMemory with -1 returned as 0, then memset to zero over the block's size from the header at payload-4, less 8. A block from X32_AllocMemory has no header, so that size is read from the 4 bytes before it.

entries.name: Context_GetTransform
entries.description: (context), callee-cleaned: the rotation an object's orientation block holds, built on demand. When the word at +0x26 is 0 it builds the Q14 rotation at +6 from the three int16 Euler angles at +0 with BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 (0005f0ac) and sets the word to 1; it returns context + 6. Most of the calls es2_naming.py callers lists pass an object's +6. ES2's class 'Context' (0x28 bytes, no vptr; MAT_OBJ's base at +0xc) has this layout, and ES2's SimObject_InstallModelTransform (DBSIM 00401fe4) builds the matrix inline.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 000016e8, against ES2's SimObject_InstallModelTransform

entries.name: SimObject_InstallModelTransform
entries.description: (object), callee-cleaned: installs an object's orientation as the renderer's model transform: Raster_SetModelTransform(Context_GetTransform(object + 6)), Context_GetTransform building the rotation on demand. es2_xref finds 16 calls and 10 stored pointers (draw slots of object vtables). ES2's SimObject_InstallModelTransform (DBSIM 00401fe4) builds the matrix inline.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00001854, against ES2's SimObject_InstallModelTransform

entries.name: TSObj_Ctor
entries.description: (object, shape) in stack order, callee-cleaned: TS_OBJ's constructor, allocating 0x3b bytes when object is null. Installs DRAWABLE's vtable 0009020a at +2, zeroes the Context at +6 (its Euler angles at +0, its translation at +0x1a and its cached-rotation word +0x26), installs MAT_OBJ's vtable 000902ca and then TS_OBJ's 000902ea, stores TSShapeInstance_Ctor(0, shape) at +0x2e (0 for a null shape) and clears the 8 bytes at +0x32. ES2's TS_OBJ is 0x41 bytes with the shape instance at +0x34.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames
entries.description: (holder, shape) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the two-field shape-instance holder's constructor, allocating 8 bytes when holder is null. Stores the shape at +0 and, when the shape's word count +0x24 is non-zero, a copy of its word array +0x1c (Arena_Alloc from the arena 000bd954, then memmove) at +4, else 0. HeapBlockOwner_Dtor is its destructor. ES2's ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames (DBSIM 00402fc0).

entries.name: HeapBlockOwner_Dtor
entries.description: (owner, flags), callee-cleaned: operator_delete of the block at owner + 4, then of owner itself when flags bit 0 is set; returns at once for a null owner. The destructor of the holder ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames builds: destructors such as 00000338 (which ends in TSBase_Dtor) and 000028e0 run it on the holder at their +0x10 with flags 0. ES2's HeapBlockOwner_Dtor (DBSIM 00403020).

entries.name: FlatObj_LoadResources
entries.description: (selector), callee-cleaned: ES2's FlatObj_LoadResources (DBSIM 004097a8) in part. Shape_LoadAllRoots(0, 0x140008, dts\flat for a selector of 0 and dts\flat2 otherwise, &000bc1d8), the root array to 000bc1d8 and its count to 000bc1dc; then Pool_Init(0, 0x3b, 0x96), a pool of 150 elements of 0x3b bytes, to 000af044. It loads no dba bank, binds none to the shapes and builds no delete queue, as ES2's does. World_LoadTheater (000251c4) calls it last with World_FlatSetSelector (000928e2).

entries.name: Ai_SelectTarget
entries.description: (this, mask) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the AI's target acquisition. Walks the object pointer array at *000bc416 (count int16 000bc41c, a null entry ending it) and returns the best-scoring candidate, or 0. A candidate must pass 0000dce8(this, mask, candidate). The group (+0x3f) designates it when 0001ce3c(group, candidate) holds and the group's word +4 is 1. A candidate with its byte +0x9e set is skipped unless the group designates it and the group's byte +0x14 is set. Its tier is 2 * d + 1, less 1 when any of its bytes +0x9f, +0x9e and +0x93 is set, d being 1 when the group designates it or mask bit 0 is clear; one below the tier bar (0 at the start) is skipped. Score: b = 0x1000 - (|bearing error| >> 3), the error being the heading from this +0x20 to the candidate's +0x20 (Math_HeadingToward) less this's heading +0xa, 0 with mask 0x20; Q10(100, b), raised inside a Math_DistanceBetweenPoints range of 25000 to b / max(range >> 11, 1) when that is larger; then Q10-multiplied by the weight tables 00091620 (candidate's +0x15e is this, unless mask bit 1), 00091628 (candidate's behaviour descriptor byte +9 clear), 00091630 (candidate's +0x15e is another object) and 00091638 (by the candidate's int16 +0x162), the first three indexed by this's vtable +0x50 (this, candidate); and divided by one more than the candidate's holders +0x15c, less one when this's +0x15e is the candidate, unless mask bit 2. A higher score or a higher tier replaces the best and sets the bar to its tier. ES2's Ai_SelectTarget (DBSIM 00411fa0) adds the cone limit and the range caps, scores Q10(70, b) and b / (range >> 12) inside 60000, and adds the locally-piloted test and the own-class mask bit.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 0000ddf4, against ES2's Ai_SelectTarget

entries.name: Behaviour_SetState
entries.description: (block, descriptor) in stack order, callee-cleaned: installs a behaviour state in the block a machine carries at +0x47. Stores the descriptor at +0, zeroes the int +9, adds 0xd to the int16 000bc426 and seeds the countdown +5 to descriptor +4 plus that word's low four bits, clears the 0x10 bytes at +0x35, sets +0x36 to 1 and clears the 0x28 bytes at +0xd. ES2's Behaviour_SetState (DBSIM 00413e50), whose block sits at +0x4d.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0000fdfc, against ES2's Behaviour_SetState

entries.name: Behaviour_BuildStateTable
entries.description: Static constructor (its pointer is at 000adbf4, in the XI range __cinit walks) that fills the 20 behaviour state descriptors of BehaviourStateTable (000af26c): name, dwell, the 16-bit flag mask expanded by Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, the think, move and reassess functions and the closing dword. The states, in order: deciding, player, attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer, patrolling, travelling, bulldog travel, search destroy, sleeping, skirting, guarding, driving off en, ramming, fleeing, in limbo, dead, disabled. Dwell is 50000 for the five combat states and driving off en, 30000 for fleeing, 0 for deciding, dead and disabled, and 10 otherwise. ES2's Behaviour_BuildStateTable (DBSIM 00413ed4) builds 22.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0000fee4, against ES2's Behaviour_BuildStateTable

entries.name: Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits
entries.description: (out, mask) in stack order, callee-cleaned: unpacks the low 16 bits of *mask into 16 bytes, bit i & 1 into out[i]. Behaviour_BuildStateTable runs it on each descriptor's +8. ES2's Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits (DBSIM 00415028).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00010578, against ES2's Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits

entries.name: Mech_LocomotionTick
entries.description: (mech, avoidance arg, desired speed, steer) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the HERC control law and gait machine, with the type record at +0x188. An immobilised machine (+0x9e) has desired speed and steer zeroed. Otherwise, while 00064178(mech + 0x203) reports the timer running, the desired speed becomes the type's +4 when +0xa8 is set and +6 when not; once it reports 0 the desired speed is clamped to [+4, +6]. A machine other than the player (000bc42a) that is not immobilised runs 00011c80. Damage scales the desired speed by Q10 400 (+0xa3) or 750 (+0xa2), steer is clamped to +/-0x100, and the speed +0x224 moves toward the desired speed by typeRec +8 (Math_RateLimitedMoveToward). The gait machine then compares |speed| with last tick's on the locomotion thread +0x1c0, cutting to or requesting the type's sequences +0xe, +0x10, +0x12, +0x14, +0x46 and +0x7c with AnimThread_SetSequence (0006200c) and AnimThread_SetTarget (0006265c) and setting the playback rate +0x236: an immobilised machine off +0x7c falls to +0x46, requesting it at rate 100 with Sound_PlayAt 0x1e at +0x20 unless +0xae is latched, then running at rate 0x78 and, once the sequence has played, latching +0xae, calling 00013078(mech, 0x78, 0x96) and playing 0x29. The turn rate +0x222 then moves by typeRec +0xa toward Q8(steer, tent): the tent is 0 when a gait branch set its step flag this tick or |speed| is below 45; otherwise it rises from 0 at 45 to typeRec +2 midway between 45 and the top speed +6, and falls to half that at the top speed. The heading +0xa takes the turn rate and +0x2c, the orientation block's cached-rotation word, is cleared. ES2's Mech_LocomotionTick (DBSIM 00416a04) adds the terrain slope, the Turbo Pod and the minimum playback rate, and peaks its tent at Q10(1600).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00012038, against ES2's Mech_LocomotionTick

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: No arguments: LoadNameList(10, 0x60, 0, 'mechs') in stack order into 000bc440; __vec_new of the int16 mech type count 000bc42e records of 0x1c4 bytes, element constructor 00019f3e, into 000bc444; 00030288(count); then for each type number from 0 to 15 whose 00019a30(type) is not 0xff, 00019cf0(type). ES2's Mechs_InitAllTypes (DBSIM 0042049c), whose table has 0x55 entries, whose records are 0x21e bytes and which walks all 0x55 type numbers.

entries.name: Computer_PostMessage
entries.description: (id), callee-cleaned: posts a message to the cockpit computer's port at CockpitViewInstance (00092d1c) + 0x207 with 0002ed94(port, record), the record's first int16 the id and its second 0. ES2's Computer_PostMessage (DBSIM 00420a68) posts through the port's vtable slot 0 at +0x20b.

entries.name: FlyerTypes_LoadAll
entries.description: No arguments: when the int16 flyer type count 000bc464 is non-zero, LoadNameList(10, 0x52, 0, 'flyers') in stack order into 000bc468; operator new of count * 0x2e bytes into 000bc46c, with no element constructor; then for type numbers 0 and 1 whose 0001c678(type) is not 0xff, 0001c6c8(type). ES2's FlyerTypes_LoadAll (DBSIM 00422fb4), which builds 0x70-byte records with an element constructor and walks 0x22 type numbers.

entries.name: DBSim_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: (): the world load's first pass over the shell's handoff, ES2's DBSim_LoadScriptDat (DBSIM 00424308) in role. Clears the roster slot arrays (000af7b4, 000af818 and 000af87c, 100 bytes each; 000af8e0, 000af914, 000af948, 000af97c and 000af9b0, 50 each); reads data\mission.var's 200 bytes into 000bc4b8 and zeroes the word at 000bc4c6; reads data\player.mec, a word to 000af9fa, a count to 000af9e2 and that many 0x7e-byte entries at 000af9e4, then 0x11 bytes to 000af9e8; opens data\script.dat (Path_WithExtension with "dat"; severity-5 assert, world.cpp line 0xb2) and reads the 20-byte header into 000bc49c, the points (12 bytes each, tracking the least and greatest X and Y at 000af7a4-000af7b0), the headings as value << 14 in 16 bits, the waypoint groups as pointers to their points, the trigger areas through FUN_0001cb48 into 10-byte records, and the actions into 16-byte records with the count of area refs up to the first negative one; of the mechs (98 bytes), flyers (56) and bases (16) it keeps only the type at +0x28, +0x2c and +0; of the groups (82 bytes) it marks, from the second record on, each member ref at +0x34 live in the roster +0x28 names, a base member also storing the group's +0x44. The player.mec entries are then marked live as mech slots after the block's count, and calls not read follow.

entries.name: Terrain_LoadZoneShapes
entries.description: (theater, zone) in stack order, callee-cleaned, terrain.cpp: loads the shapes standing on a zone. For a negative zone it zeroes Zone_ShapeCount (000bc588), Zone_TheaterShapeRoots (000bc580) and Zone_ShapeObjects (000bc584) and returns. Otherwise it builds dat\zone<zone> by ltoa (radix 10) over the XXXX of a copy of 'zoneXXXX' (000924b0) and ResourcePath_BuildFolderName, opens it with VolRStream_CtorFromPath (severity-5 assert, terrain.cpp line 0x32, when it fails), reads the word at +0 into a local it does not use again and the record count into Zone_ShapeCount. Shape_LoadAllRoots(0, 0x2bc0001, dgs\<name>, &Zone_TheaterShapeRoots), the name Terrain_TheaterNames (000924a0)[theater], gives the root count k; it reads k * 24 bytes of dat\<name> into a __vec_new array of TheaterShapeRecord_ElementCtor elements at Zone_TheaterShapeRecords (000bc58a) and closes that file. When the count is not 0 it allocates count pointers at Zone_ShapeObjects and for each 20-byte record reads a shape index (2 bytes), a position (12) and three angles (6), and builds a 0x3f-byte object: TSObj_Ctor(object, roots[index]) and the vptr 000924be at +2 (both skipped when operator_new fails, the stores below not); the angles to +6 and the position to +0x20, the orientation block's angles and translation; 0 to +0x2c; at +0x3b the address of the index's 24-byte record, or 0 when that record's int32 at +8 is negative. Neither index is tested against a count. Closes the zone file. With a count of 0, Zone_ShapeObjects is left as it was.

entries.name: TheaterShapeRecord_ElementCtor
entries.description: (this) callee-cleaned: the __vec_new element constructor Terrain_LoadZoneShapes (00020238) passes (by way of the padding entry 000204d5) for the 24-byte records of dat\<theater>. Allocates 0x18 bytes when this is null and returns null when that fails; the inlined constructors of two 0xc-byte members at +0 and +0xc, each holding an 8-byte member at +0, only repeat the null test and allocation at their own sizes. Writes nothing to the record; returns this.

entries.description: (manager), frameless, callee-cleaned: stores its argument in CockpitViewManagerPublished (000bc5a0). 0005a9dc passes the dword at 000b5b60. ES2's CockpitViewManager_Publish (DBSIM 00429810).

entries.description: Frameless: returns CockpitViewManagerPublished (000bc5a0). The callers es2_naming.py callers lists read the view manager's +0x10 (compared with 4), the byte +0x18 and the pointer +0x1b, where ES2's manager has the current view at +0x14, a byte at +0x1c and the CockpitView widget tree at +0x1f. entries.description: (manager), callee-cleaned: returns the dword at manager + 0x1b, where ES2's CockpitViewManager_GetCockpitView (DBSIM 00429828) returns +0x1f, the CockpitView widget tree.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_QueueViewCommand
entries.description: (manager, command) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while no command is pending (+0x14 is -1), stores a command the current view +0x10 allows: 0 from view 0, 1 from view 1, 2 from any view but 4, 3 from view 4; 4 stored as 4 from view 0 and as 6 from view 3; 5 stored as 5 from view 0 and as 6 from view 2; 6 from views 2 and 3. Any other pair leaves +0x14 as it was. ES2's manager keeps its pending view command at +0x18.

entries.name: CockpitView_GetShakeOffset
entries.description: No arguments: sets the byte 000afdb0 to 1 and returns a pointer to the static int pair at 000afdb4, written as {0, (int)(short)000afb6c}. Sim_RenderFrame adds the pair into the render context's +0x220/+0x224 for the frame and takes it out after. ES2's CockpitView_GetShakeOffset (DBSIM 0042d870).

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
entries.description: (header), callee-cleaned: ES2's World_LoadTheater (DBSIM 0042e010) for ES1's world file. DBSim_LoadScriptDat (0001d850) passes data\script.dat's 20-byte header (000bc49c); it copies it to 000bc5a4. With t header word 0, v word 9 and d word 8 it loads dpl\world<6t+2v> with Palette_LoadAndActivate (00027e5c) and opens wld\world<6t+2v+d>. Hzline_Ctor (00026180) builds g_TheaterHzline (000928d4); of the file's twelve leading int16 (ES2 reads fourteen), 0-7 go to the hzline as ES2's do (+0x6c, +0x54, +0x58, +0x5c, +0x60, and Hzline_SetColors (00026234) with 1, 4 and 7), short4 + short6 - 1 to 000928e0, short 8 to a local, 9 to World_FlatSetSelector (000928e2), 10 and 11 to 000bc5d0 and 000bc5d2; 000bc5ce = 0x40, 000bc5d4 = 0x62. Two int32-counted int32 tables to WorldShades_BandsTagged (000afdc4) and WorldShades_BandsTag0 (000afdc8), counts' low halves at 000bc5b8 and 000bc5ba; rows and cols int16 to 000bc5be and 000bc5bc; two cols x 4-byte range tables (64-byte stack buffers, cols unchecked) around an unused int16 expanded by Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges (000289e0) into WorldShades_LevelRanges (000afdbc), then two 4-byte ranges into WorldShades_BlendRanges (000afdc0); int16 cloud count, int16 point count, two int32 to WorldShades_DistanceOffsets (000bc5c6). Five NUL-terminated strings read a byte at a time, unbounded, into 12-byte stack buffers: the first, when not empty, to Hzline_LoadBitmapBank (00026dc8); the second, when not empty, a 0x113-byte object built by maybe_Clouds_Ctor (000271c0) with the cloud count, vptr 000928f6, into World_Clouds (000928d8); the third, when not empty, Palette_LoadDpl(dpl\<name>) into ImpactPaletteObject (000928f0); the fourth and fifth to GndTex_Load. A non-zero point count builds PointScatter_Ctor (00026dec) into World_PointScatter (000928dc), with short 8 at its +0x15. Closes the file; opens cyc\world<6t+2v+d> with VolRStream_Open and, when it opens with a non-zero int16 count (000928e8), allocates 6 x count bytes (000928e4) and reads count records of three int16 at a 12-byte stride, registering each with PaletteCycle_Register (000281cc). World_LoadShades (00025bc8) with 'shades'; GndTex_Load (00028de8) with (fifth string, fourth string, short 0, short 5, short 6, short 4) in stack order; FlatObj_LoadResources (00006cf8) with World_FlatSetSelector; destroys the stream. No rmp file, Terrain_BindTextureBank or Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions, where ES2 has them.

entries.name: World_LoadShades
entries.description: (name), callee-cleaned: ES2's World_LoadShades (DBSIM 0042e760): dat\<name> as a count byte N (into 000bc5c4), N zeroed 5-byte records {byte count, pointer} at WorldShades_TypeTable (000bc5c0), then a byte K and K entries {record index, count, count two-byte pairs into a new array on that record}. The type table WorldShades_ApplyForObject reads in ES2. World_LoadTheater (000251c4) calls it through the padding entry 00025bc6 with 'shades'.

entries.name: Hzline_Ctor
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: ES2's Hzline_Ctor (DBSIM 0042eb5c). Allocates 0x71 bytes for a null this (ES2's object is 0x7a), calls the base constructor 000547b4, stores the vptr 00092aaa and the defaults +0x6c = 1, +0x54 = 3, +0x58 = 16, +0x5c = 1, +0x60 = 8, +0x64 = +0x68 = 1, +0x50 = 0, and the byte +0x70 = 1, where ES2 stores 0 at +0x70 and 1 at +0x71.

entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `vsprintf`, from `printf.c`: (buffer, format, args), C convention: formats through _pformat (0005f7ca) with Printf_StoreChar and a cursor on buffer, then stores a NUL at buffer plus the formatter's result, or at buffer itself when the result is negative.

entries.name: _pformat
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `_pformat`, from `printf.c`: (output, stream, format, args), C convention: the formatter vprintf, vfprintf and vsprintf share. Sends each character through output(c, stream) and returns the count sent, or -1 when output returns -1 or a conversion is not in its table. The flag characters are the table 00097ddc ('-', '+', ' ', '#', '0', '*'), digits are tested through the ctype table 0009edc5, and the conversions are the 18-entry table 00097e14 (s % c d i b o u p X x f F e E G g n), each with a handler address 0x48 bytes on; 6.1's printf.c reads F as a size modifier instead. entries.description: (row, label, hundredths, whole) in stack order, callee-cleaned: prints label and a rate on a monochrome-screen row with Mono_PrintfRow, as "%s%2d.%02d fps." entries.description: No arguments, frameless: decrements FrameRate_Countdown (000b5e24) while it is non-zero. FrameRate_Update registers it with Timer_AddCallback (0006d289), count 1.

entries.name: FrameRate_GetFrameCount
entries.description: No arguments, frameless: returns FrameRate_FrameCount (000b5e28). 00000c84, in vcr.cpp, passes it to sprintf for its "Playback error. Frame #%ld" message.

entries.name: FrameRate_Update
entries.description: No arguments: the frame-rate meter, called once a frame. On its first call (FrameRate_TicksPerSecond FrameRate_TicksPerSecond (000b5e2c) is 0) it registers FrameRate_TimerTick with Timer_AddCallback (0006d289) at count 1, sets the ticks per second to 1000000 / Math_Q14Multiply(word +4 of the structure 000bdd0c points to, 0x35a1), loads FrameRate_Countdown (000b5e24) with 32000 and returns. Later calls take the ticks elapsed, e = 32000 - countdown, and reload it. e = 32000 prints "Current: Slower than %d fps." (00097f54) with 32000 / ticks per second on row 4. Otherwise, for e above the ticks per second, x = 10e / ticks per second and the rate shown is x / 10 and x % 10 as whole and hundredths, the seconds per frame in tenths printed as frames per second; for any other e, x = 100 * ticks per second / e, or 99999 when e is 0, and the rate is x / 100 and x % 100, which raises the best (FrameRate_Best (00097f58), whole then hundredths) when it is higher and neither 999 nor 99 hundredths, and lowers the worst (FrameRate_Worst (00097f5c)) when it is lower. It prints "Best:" on row 3 and "Worst:" on row 5 with FrameRate_PrintRate, then on row 4 "Current: Faster than %d fps." (00097f2c) with the ticks per second when x is 99999, or "Current:" and the rate. Each call after the first adds 1 to FrameRate_FrameCount (000b5e28) and prints "Frame # %d" on row 1. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.description: byte: bit n-1 set when MECMODn.DYN opened, written by MechMods_Probe. No reader found by a search of the disassembly for the address.

entries.name: Mono_Screen
entries.description: 2 bytes, built by MonoScreen_Ctor at startup: +0 is 1 when Crtc_DetectDualDisplay found both adapters, +1 is 1. Mono_Clear, Mono_WriteChar, Mono_WriteText, Mono_Printf, Mono_PrintScreen and Mono_ShowCursor do their work only while the two bytes share a set bit.

entries.name: g_ModelToView
entries.description: The current model-to-view transform (0x20 bytes), built by Raster_SetModelTransform. ES2's g_ModelToView (DBSIM 006c6038).

entries.name: g_ViewToModel
entries.description: The inverse of g_ModelToView, built by Raster_SetModelTransform. ES2's g_ViewToModel (DBSIM 006c6058).

entries.name: Transform_Identity
entries.description: The identity transform Raster_SetModelTransform and Raster_SetViewTransform install for a null pointer. ES2's DBSIM 006c6080.

entries.name: g_EyeInModelSpace
entries.description: The viewpoint in the current model's space (three ints): the origin through g_ViewToModel, written by Raster_SetModelTransform. ES2's g_EyeInModelSpace (DBSIM 006c60a0).

entries.name: Raster_ProjectionCentre
entries.description: The projection centre, two int32: the camera's clip rect's top-left less its render context's +0x220 pair (Raster_InstallViewProjection). ES2's DBSIM 006c60b8.

entries.name: Raster_ViewClipRect
entries.description: The installed camera's clip rect, four int32 copied from its render context's +0x210..+0x21c by Raster_InstallViewProjection. ES2's DBSIM 006c60c0.

entries.name: PolyFill_LineBrush
entries.description: The poly renderers' line brush: its mode at +0 and PolyFill_LineColour (000b5efc) at +4. Light_ResetSystem (000632ec) zeroes the mode. ES2's PolyFill_LineBrush (DBSIM 006c60d0).

entries.name: PolyFill_LineColour
entries.description: The polygon renderers' line colour; PolyFill_Fill and PolyFill_FillThenOutline draw an outline in it when it differs from the brush colour. ES2's DBSIM 006c60d4.

entries.name: PolyFill_FillBrush
entries.description: The polygon renderers' fill brush: +0 the mode, +4 the colour (000b5f04). ES2's DBSIM PolyFill_FillBrush (006c60d8).

entries.name: Poly_VertexCount
entries.description: The current polygon's vertex count (uint16), the start of the polygon scratch block, whose fields keep ES2's offsets from DBSIM 006c6968.

entries.name: Poly_IndexOffset
entries.description: The current polygon's offset into Poly_IndexList (uint16). ES2's DBSIM 006c696a.

entries.name: Poly_ShortPoints
entries.description: Pointer to the shape's int16 point triples, which Poly_ProjectShapeVertices projects. ES2's DBSIM 006c696c.

entries.name: Poly_IntPoints
entries.description: Pointer to the int32 point triples Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices and Poly_ProjectViewVertices project. ES2's DBSIM 006c6970.

entries.name: Poly_IndexList
entries.description: Pointer to the vertex-index list, uint16 point numbers. ES2's DBSIM 006c6976.

entries.name: Poly_PointState
entries.description: One byte per point, 1000: 0 not yet seen, 1 behind the near plane, 2 projected. ES2's DBSIM 006c697e.

entries.name: Poly_ViewCache
entries.description: 1000 int32 {x, y, z} view-space points; the projectors store each vertex's transformed point here and the near-plane clips interpolate from it. ES2's DBSIM Poly_ViewCache (006c6d66).

entries.name: Poly_ScreenCache
entries.description: 1000 int32 {x, y} screen points, each projected vertex's, copied for a point marked 2. ES2's DBSIM Poly_ScreenCache (006c9c46).

entries.name: Poly_ScreenPoints
entries.description: The ring to fill: 32 int32 {x, y} screen points, count at Poly_ScreenCount. ES2's DBSIM Poly_ScreenPoints (006cbb86).

entries.name: Poly_ScreenCount
entries.description: The ring's point count (uint16), set by the projectors and the near-plane clips. ES2's DBSIM 006cbc86.

entries.name: Zone_TheaterShapeRoots
entries.description: Pointer to the array of root shapes Shape_LoadAllRoots loads from the theater's dgs\<name> in Terrain_LoadZoneShapes (00020238); a zone's 20-byte records index it. Null after a load with a negative zone.

entries.name: Zone_ShapeObjects
entries.description: Pointer to the array of Zone_ShapeCount (000bc588) object pointers Terrain_LoadZoneShapes (00020238) builds, one 0x3f-byte object (TS_OBJ and a pointer at +0x3b, vptr 000924be) per zone record. Null after a load with a negative zone; a load with a count of 0 leaves it as it was.

entries.name: Zone_ShapeCount
entries.description: int16: the zone file's record count (its word at +2), the number of objects at Zone_ShapeObjects (000bc584). Terrain_LoadZoneShapes (00020238) reads it, or sets 0 for a negative zone.

entries.name: Zone_TheaterShapeRecords
entries.description: Pointer to the theater's 24-byte shape records, one per root shape, read from dat\<name> by Terrain_LoadZoneShapes (00020238) into a __vec_new array of TheaterShapeRecord_ElementCtor (000204d8) elements. A zone object's +0x3b points at its shape's record unless that record's int32 at +8 is negative.

entries.name: CockpitViewManagerPublished
entries.description: The cockpit view manager, stored by CockpitViewManager_Publish and returned by CockpitViewManager_Published. Widget_DrawToCockpit tests its byte +0x18. ES2's CockpitViewManagerPublished (DBSIM 004cfa20).

entries.name: WorldShades_TypeTable
entries.description: Pointer to the 5-byte records {byte count, pointer to count two-byte pairs} World_LoadShades (00025bc8) reads from dat\shades, the record count byte at 000bc5c4. ES2's WorldShades_TypeTable (DBSIM 004cfd64).

entries.name: WorldShades_DistanceOffsets
entries.description: Two int32, 000bc5c6 and 000bc5ca, read from the world file after its two counts by World_LoadTheater (000251c4). ES2's WorldShades_DistanceOffsets (DBSIM 004cfd6c).

entries.name: Raster_ViewTransformPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the installed view transform, written by Raster_SetViewTransform. ES2's DBSIM 006c6078.

entries.name: g_ModelTransformPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the installed model transform, the identity at Transform_Identity (000b5eb4) when null is installed; written by Raster_SetModelTransform. ES2's g_ModelTransformPtr (DBSIM 006c607c).

entries.name: Raster_FocalShift
entries.description: The installed camera's focal shift (+0x1a): the projection is (x << shift) / depth, and 0 selects the orthographic form. ES2's DBSIM 006c60ac.

entries.name: Raster_NearPlane
entries.description: The installed camera's near-plane depth (+0x1e). ES2's DBSIM 006c60b0.

entries.name: Raster_OrthoDivisor
entries.description: The installed camera's orthographic divisor (+0x22), set only when the focal shift is 0. ES2's DBSIM 006c60b4.

entries.name: Light_ActiveCount
entries.description: Number of entries in Light_ActiveList. ES2's DBSIM 006c612c.

entries.name: Light_ActiveList
entries.description: The active light list, ten light pointers, which the shade functions walk. ES2's DBSIM 006c6130.

entries.name: Light_ModelSpaceEnabled
entries.description: Byte: when set, Raster_SetModelTransform moves each registered light into the model's space and the save and restore carry the lights' copies. ES2's DBSIM 006cbc88.

entries.name: Bitmap_UseCallerScratch
entries.description: Flag Bitmap_Blit tests after drawing a packed bitmap: while it is 0 the blit deletes Bitmap_UnpackScratch. ES2's Bitmap_UseCallerScratch (DBSIM 006c5ff8).

entries.name: Bitmap_UnpackScratch
entries.description: The buffer a packed bitmap is unpacked into for drawing: Bitmap_Blit puts it in the bitmap's data pointer +0xe for the blit and deletes it afterwards unless Bitmap_UseCallerScratch is set. ES2's Bitmap_UnpackScratch (DBSIM 006c5ffc).
